submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole fires on tokens inside text that is reproduced rather than composed: machine-generated strings (source code and config, patch/diff lines, base64 hashes inside <script integrity=...> tags, LaTeX/markdown citation markup such as [@cit0008] or ](…){#sp1}) and formulaic legal/web boilerplate (copyright and licence headers, cookie-consent notices, blog footers, event agendas) - with its hardest peaks on tokens that are themselves fragments of those strings ('ab' and 'ma' inside a sha384 hash, the '2' of '129 Cal. Rptr.', '(),' closing a Django url(...) call, 'OrUpdate' inside a generated Go identifier). Ordinary narrative prose, and plain-English rewrites of the same formulae, stay at or near zero; the pole's output direction reads as the locative preposition 'in'/在 but it prepares no specific upcoming token (measured is_lookahead = false, KL ~ 3e-6), so the claim is retrospective.

Q:

Django ModelForm not showing up in template

I've been using django for a couple of days now and I'm trying to create a small app to learn the whole stuff.
I've read about the ModelForms and I wanted to use it in my app, but I can't get it to render in my template and I can't find the problem, so I was hoping you guys could help me out.
Here's my code:
models.py
from django.db import models

class Kiss(models.Model):
    latitude    = models.FloatField()
    longitude   = models.FloatField()
    person1     = models.CharField(max_length = 255)
    person2     = models.CharField(max_length = 255)
    cdate       = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    def __unicode__(self):
        return self.person1

views.py
from django.views.generic.list import ListView
from project.models import Kiss
from project.forms import KissForm
from django.http import HttpResponseRedirect

class KissListView(ListView):
    template_name = 'project/home.html'
    model = Kiss
    form = KissForm

urls.py (only the relevant part)
urlpatterns += patterns('',
         url(r'^$', KissListView.as_view(), name='home'),
     )

forms.py
from django import forms
from project.models import Kiss

class KissForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
         model = Kiss

and the template
<form action="" method="POST">
            {% csrf_token %}
            {{form.as_p}}
            <button>Send</button>
        </form>

Thanks in advance for your help.
J

A:

class KissListView(ListView):
...

You are using ListView which does not require form and will not give you form in the template context.
You may want to use CreateView instead.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Long before the road was built, the only way to reach the village was by water, and the people who lived there measured the year by which boats came and which did not. My grandmother kept a ledger of them in a hand she never quite made neat: the name of the boat, the name of the man, the weather, the day. She was not a sentimental person and she did not write down what she felt about any of it. The ledger was a record, and records, she said, are for other people.

I found it in a cupboard after she died, under a stack of tablecloths that still smelled faintly of her kitchen. For a long time I did nothing with it. I was busy, or I told myself I was busy, and there is a kind of grief that only becomes available when you stop moving, which I was not ready to do. Then one winter the power went out for four days, and I sat down with the ledger and began to copy the entries into a notebook of my own.

The first thing I noticed was how many of the boats had names that meant nothing to me. The second was how often she had written the word same in the weather column, as though the sea had been too dull to describe. She was, I think, making a joke that only she would get, and she was making it in a document she expected no one to read. That is a particular kind of humour, and it may be the best kind.

The village is different now. There is a car park where the slipway used to be, a cafe that serves coffee in cups too large to finish, and a sign explaining that the harbour was once the busiest on this stretch of coast. The sign is accurate in the way that signs are accurate: everything it says is true and none of it is the point. My grandmother would have read it and said nothing, which from her was a full review.

I finished copying the entries in the spring. It took longer than it should have, because I kept stopping to check whether a name forty pages back was the same person, and because the handwriting changed in small ways I had not expected, as though the hand itself had aged in the margins. When it was done I put the notebook in the cupboard beside the ledger and closed the door. I have not opened either since. But I think about those four days of darkness more often than I think about most things, and I have begun to suspect that the copying was not for her at all.

The sources for this piece were recorded in the journal's house style:

As the parish registers make clear \citep{trevose1978harbour}, and as the later survey of coastal trade confirms \citep{pasco2004boats}, the harbour stayed active until the 1930s \citep[see][pp.~44--61]{hocking1991west}. The ledger itself is held at the county archive \citep{nancarrow2012ledger}; its entries are discussed at length in \citet{trevose2014copies}. See Section~\ref{sec:provenance} and Table~\ref{tab:entries} for the full inventory.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout: about 600 tokens of composed narrative with LaTeX \citep/\ref markup only at the very end, where the hypothesis predicts the peak.
